football_evidence.question: Can North Dakota State’s pass rush get to UTEP’s quarterback?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward North Dakota State, and its own breakdown accounts for about 1.3 of the 4.5 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When North Dakota State has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): North Dakota State’s offense has allowed a sack on 5.1% of its dropbacks, and UTEP’s defense sacks the quarterback on 3.4% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).

When UTEP has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): UTEP’s offense has allowed a sack on 18.3% of its dropbacks, and North Dakota State’s defense sacks the quarterback on 7.8% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).
When UTEP has the ball (third down): UTEP’s offense converts 28.4% of its third downs, and North Dakota State’s defense allows opponents to convert 34.3% of their third downs (FBS average 39.5%).

When UTEP has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): UTEP’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 17.9% of its runs, and North Dakota State’s defense stops 20.7% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.5%).
contradicting: In his last two games (Nevada and New Mexico), Hayes averaged 6.1 yards per attempt, against 8.1 in his six games before that.
In his last two games (Nevada and San José State), Moore averaged 6.1 yards per attempt, against 4.3 in his four games before that.
EdgeDesk’s position-group ratings put UTEP’s running backs No. 55 nationally and North Dakota State’s No. 138.

When North Dakota State has the ball (the red zone): North Dakota State’s offense succeeds on 39.5% of its red-zone plays, and UTEP’s defense allows success on 38.1% of opponent red-zone plays (FBS average 43.6%).
quarterbacks: Nathan Hayes has completed 123 of 196 passes (62.8%) for 1,470 yards, 7.5 yards per attempt, 12 touchdowns and 7 interceptions in eight games for North Dakota State, and has been sacked on 10 of 206 dropbacks.
EJ Colson Jr. has completed 54 of 82 passes (65.9%) for 615 yards, 7.5 yards per attempt, 6 touchdowns and 3 interceptions in six games for UTEP, and has been sacked on 19 of 101 dropbacks.
Raymond Moore III has completed 44 of 72 passes (61.1%) for 405 yards, 5.6 yards per attempt, 2 touchdowns and 2 interceptions in six games for UTEP, and has been sacked on 15 of 87 dropbacks.
